title: ECS broker jobs
description: The closed table of the lean ECS broker. A step names its job, or null when the broker answers it without a task. A job names its deadline, the container whose log the logs route shows and the variables each container receives.

chain.description: The job belongs to the bronze-triggered chain and runs only after the first silver and gold publishes are signed

after.description: The job whose succeeded run the request's input_run_id must name

acceptance.description: Containers that hold the acceptance checks. Each must be in the task's report and exit 0

needs_bronze_request.description: The run stages bronze_request.json beside its code archive. The broker reads and checks it before it starts the task and passes its values to the containers

needs_bronze_code.description: The run stages nothing and reads no request: it runs the code of its bronze run (the code of its ingestion run, bound once at its launch) and writes the bronze run's request and source inventory itself. The launch preflight binds the run to that code and gives the containers only the run ID and the code values

needs_publisher_run_request.description: The run names its kind (bootstrap or monthly) and its capture root as launch parameters and stages nothing but its code archive. The direct launch preflight checks them before it starts the Run 3 publisher task, binds every attempt to their digest and passes them to the run container

needs_serving_parameters.description: The launch form carries a closed serving request: the infection type and the mode, canary or stable. The launch preflight derives the candidate version from the type's research record and fixes the canary share from canary_percent, so the serve container receives a checked request and no caller names a version or a share

canary_percent.description: The share of hospital-windows a canary deployment receives, fixed here and never named by a caller. A job with needs_serving_parameters must set it

canary_ttl_hours.description: The hours a canary deployment serves its share, counted from its write: the deployment record carries the expiry, and the model API serves the canary only before it. Fixed here and never named by a caller. A job with needs_serving_parameters must set it
